ideas.idea: Give each mug its own page/URL linked from the catalogue (with product structured data)
ideas.why:
Catalogue.jsx renders mugs as plain

text with no links, so individual products have no addressable pages.

ideas.idea: Add shipping, delivery and returns information in text to back up the 'shipped worldwide' claim
ideas.why: Home.jsx claims worldwide shipping but no page gives details, so adding them helps users and machines understand the offer.

ideas.idea: Add a viewport meta tag in index.html
ideas.why: index.html does lack it and it helps mobile rendering, but it applies to nearly every site and has little effect on being found.

ideas.idea: Link from Home content to the catalogue
ideas.why: Home.jsx has no in-content link to /catalogue, and the only route is the nav, so a real link improves discovery.

ideas.idea: Use a head helper such as react-helmet-async for per-page titles and descriptions
ideas.why: Both routes share one static title in index.html, so per-route head management is a concrete fix, though it overlaps with the known title issue.

ideas.idea: Add a canonical link tag once the domain is known
ideas.why: Accurate but the report itself says it can't tell what it should be, and it is standard advice for any site.

ideas.idea: Prerender at build time or move to a server-rendering framework for the catalogue data too
ideas.why: Catalogue.jsx fetches /api/mugs client-side, so the product list needs to be in prerendered HTML to be seen by non-JS crawlers.
